sections.heading: Customer Service Agent: Toward Autonomous Resolution
bullets: We built the foundational infrastructure for autonomous operation this period, introducing an auto-actions system with kill switches and a dashboard panel that gives the founder visibility into any action the agent executes automatically. This is a key step from the fully supervised drafting mode we started with toward genuine autonomous ticket resolution (Objective 1).

We developed an auto-send capability in a deliberately cautious, staged way: first a shadow phase that marks tickets and produces a dry-run digest without sending, then an allowlist panel and configuration controls that let the founder enable auto-send only for specific ticket categories. Sends whose proposed action was never actually executed are blocked, which prevents the agent from replying as though it had done something it had not.

We established a two-advisor architecture in which one agent drafts a response and a second closeness-to-final judge scores how close that draft is to a send-ready reply. We wired this judge into a daily quality line and a baseline runner, giving us an objective, repeatable measure of draft quality to track progress against our resolution target.

We built the operator agent that takes concrete ticket-level actions (exchanges, refunds, address changes, order creation), including deterministic confirm-button behaviour, conversation history preserved across completed actions, and stale-state cleanup. We hardened its reliability with explicit timeouts and abort-on-disconnect handling.

We captured manual-send and steer (founder-edit) events into a feedback log and added a grade-divergence flag that compares the agent's draft against the founder's edited version. This gives us the feedback loop needed to refine responses and classification over time.

sections.heading: Customer Service Agent: Reliability, Intent Routing, and Escalation
bullets: We diagnosed and resolved a significant production stability issue in which large prompts under load caused the model provider to return 529 (overloaded) errors. We built a load-shed circuit breaker that gracefully degrades from the enforced structured-output (json_schema) mode to a legacy mode when overload is detected, and made drafts fail fast rather than hang. Enforced structured output was identified as the main latency and error cause, so this work directly protects autonomous operation under real traffic.

We strengthened escalation-to-human logic so that malformed or degenerate model output is routed to a person rather than sent, and we closed several prompt loopholes (for example, ensuring required tool calls cannot be skipped). This is the confidence and edge-case handling that Objective 1 depends on.

We improved intent handling and routing accuracy: wrong-size exchanges are no longer misclassified as duplicate tickets, price-difference exchanges are correctly labelled and routed to a single return-credit invoice, and duplicate-ticket auto-close is now gated to first contact only. We also refined the deterministic price-difference and refund calculations, including correct handling of bundled and duplicate line items.

We built out ticket intake and lifecycle handling, including replying to the original customer when staff forward an email, capturing inline images as attachments, auto-resolving drift and dead-letter noise, and replaying failed intake events. A ticket-drift detector now runs hourly to catch state that has diverged.

We calibrated brand tone in several ways: the agent no longer mirrors customer complaints back at them, reciprocates genuine compliments rather than over-correcting, and follows an explicit greeting format. Remaining work centres on validating autonomous resolution and intent-classification accuracy against the held-out historical ticket set.

sections.heading: Partner Channel Discovery and Outreach
bullets: We built the core outreach engine for partner channel growth in a staged, eight-step plan with sending hard-gated off by default. This included message schemas, cadence and signal evaluators, a two-phase send function, a six-tier queue, reply correlation, and a periodic sweep job, all validated by a two-advisor draft-and-judge structure similar to the customer service side (Objective 2).

We developed the prospect discovery and qualification groundwork: a pre-filter that uses a lightweight model (Haiku) to triage an unprocessed prospect backlog, followed by a fuller research step over the candidates that survive the pre-filter. Backlog research this period produced 41 qualified prospects plus 144 community organizations.

We seeded and backfilled partner relationship state from existing status and order history, bringing 12 live organization relationships into the new business-to-business (B2B) data tables as a prerequisite for automated cadence tracking.

We surfaced the outreach work in the shared dashboard with a dedicated outreach queue panel and console tools (queue view, draft, and send), and registered the B2B outreach tools on the internal tool server. Automated sending remains intentionally disabled pending further validation, and precision scoring against manual expert review is still ahead of us.

sections.heading: Partner Onboarding and Retail Presence
bullets: We adjusted the wholesale pricing mechanism to lock partner prices via a direct price override rather than discount codes, and set non-US wholesale destinations to default to expedited shipping. These are steps toward reliable, automated partner order handling (Objective 2).

We built a store locator system, including a map-based storefront page with geolocation and B2B retail partner listings, plus the supporting tools to publish and normalize store data. This gives our growing retail partners public visibility and is currently populated with 7 active stores.

sections.heading: Growth Intelligence and Shared Platform Infrastructure
bullets: We began the growth intelligence data pipeline by standing up a Traffic and Conversion Intelligence initiative built on a Google Analytics 4 export into BigQuery, the first step toward the unified, multi-source ingestion pipeline described in Objective 3. This work is at an early stage.

We developed a weekly marketing and content/SEO loop command and an email reporting system with audience and session feeds, moving toward the automated weekly narrative summaries envisioned for the decision intelligence dashboard.

We built an inventory projection and production-order engine for merchandising, including a multi-stage order flow from the projections sheet, data-driven supplier mapping, per-color and per-SKU override handling, and generated supplier order sheets and emails. This extends the shared internal tool and database layer that the agent workflows are built on.

We invested in shared platform reliability and safety across all three objectives: a monthly bill-versus-ledger reconciliation against the model provider's admin API (with corrected model pricing), a worktree workflow that isolates concurrent autonomous sessions and is now enforced by commit hooks, and consolidated action-ledger and note-lifecycle handling so automated actions are tracked and stale alerts self-resolve.

We continued to run the free-swimwear community program inside the platform, adding repeat and duplicate applicant handling at intake, timezone-independent scheduling, and verified email sending. Much of this month's effort went into diagnosing and fixing production stability and mobile dashboard issues, which slowed net-new feature progress on the growth intelligence objective in particular.
